title: Part 4 Practice: Theories of Ethnicity: Primordialism & Instrumentalism

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three major theories of ethnicity mentioned in the module?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Out of the debate, three important theoretical perspectives emerged. These are the Primordialist, Instrumentalist, and Constructivist approaches.' Functionalism is not one of them.

questions.text: What is the core argument of Primordialism regarding ethnicity?
options: A) Ethnicity is a rational choice made for political gain.
B) Ethnicity is fixed, natural, innate, and ascribed at birth based on deep ties of kinship and culture.
C) Ethnicity is a social construct that changes over time.
D) Ethnicity is irrelevant in modern society.
questions.correct_answer: B) Ethnicity is fixed, natural, innate, and ascribed at birth based on deep ties of kinship and culture.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Primordialism is an "objectivist or essentialist theory" it argues, that "ultimately there is some real, tangible, foundation for ethnic identification."'

questions.text: Which German Romantic philosopher is a precursor to Primordialist thinking?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The Primordialist thinking can be traced back to the German Romantic philosophers, such as J.G. Herder (1744–1803), who stated the primacy of emotions and language.'

questions.text: According to Clifford Geertz, what are 'primordial attachments' based on?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'An anthropologist, Clifford Geertz (1973) systematized the primordial model. He articulated ethnicity as a natural phenomenon with its foundations in primordial ties deriving from kinship, locality, and culture.'

questions.text: What does Anthony D. Smith's 'myth-symbol complex' refer to?
options: B) The myths, memories, values, symbols, and styles that form the psychological and emotional core of ethnicity.
C) Political strategies for ethnic mobilization.
D) Biological traits of ethnic groups.
questions.correct_answer: B) The myths, memories, values, symbols, and styles that form the psychological and emotional core of ethnicity.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'According to him, the 'core' of ethnicity resides in the myths, memories, values, symbols, and the characteristic styles of particular historic configurations, i.e., what he calls 'a myth-symbol complex'.'

questions.text: What is the core argument of Instrumentalism regarding ethnicity?
options: A) Ethnicity is fixed and unchangeable.
B) Ethnicity is situational, rational, and a tool for group mobilization to gain political and economic ends.
questions.correct_answer: B) Ethnicity is situational, rational, and a tool for group mobilization to gain political and economic ends.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The instrumentalist theorists view ethnicity as situationally defined, depending on rational calculations of advantage... an instrument of group mobilization for political and economic ends.'

questions.text: According to Abner Cohen, what is the ethnic group primarily seen as?
options: B) A collectively organized strategy for the protection of economic and political interests.
D) A random collection of individuals.
questions.correct_answer: B) A collectively organized strategy for the protection of economic and political interests.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Abner Cohen (1974) placed a greater emphasis on the ethnic group as a collectively organized strategy for the protection of economic and political interests.'

questions.text: How do instrumentalist theorists view political leaders in relation to ethnicity?
options: A) Leaders have no role in ethnicity.
B) Leaders use and manipulate perceptions of ethnic identity to further their own ends and stay in power.
D) Leaders are not involved in ethnicity.
questions.correct_answer: B) Leaders use and manipulate perceptions of ethnic identity to further their own ends and stay in power.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'In the contexts of modern states, leaders (political elites) use and manipulate perceptions of ethnic identity to further their own ends and stay in power.'

questions.text: What two claims does Primordialism make according to Anthony D. Smith?
options: A) Ethnicity is political and economic.
B) Ethnicity and ethnic attachment are natural and innate, and they are ancient and perennial.
C) Ethnicity is situational and strategic.
D) Ethnicity is a modern invention.
questions.correct_answer: B) Ethnicity and ethnic attachment are natural and innate, and they are ancient and perennial.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Smith concluded that, 'primordialism' makes two distinct claims. Firstly, ethnicity and ethnic attachment are "natural and innate"... and secondly, it is "ancient and perennial".'

questions.text: In Instrumentalism, what is ethnicity ultimately regarded as?
options: B) A rational and purposive association that can be changed, constructed, or manipulated for gain.
questions.correct_answer: B) A rational and purposive association that can be changed, constructed, or manipulated for gain.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'In extreme sense, the ethnic group should be regarded not as a community at all but as a rational and purposive association. By this, ethnicity is something that can be changed, constructed, or even manipulated to gain specific political and/or economic ends.'
